questions.q: What happens when a user selects the customer account while creating a sales order?
options: Nothing, the account must be re-typed on every line
The order is automatically submitted
The customer's default bill-to/ship-to sites, payment terms, and price list become available
The order is automatically placed on credit hold
questions.explain: Selecting the customer account pulls in its defaults — sites, terms, and the applicable price list.

questions.q: What is the status of a sales order before it is submitted?
options: A draft — editable and not yet visible to downstream processes
Shipped
Closed
Invoiced
questions.explain: Before submission, the order is a draft that can be freely edited and isn't yet acted on by fulfillment or billing.

questions.q: What does submitting an order actually trigger?
options: Immediate cash collection
A General Ledger posting
Automatic deletion of the draft
Hand-off to order orchestration, which evaluates business rules like credit checks and approvals
questions.explain: Submission hands the order to orchestration, which checks rules such as credit checks and approval requirements.

questions.q: Before accepting an order line, what does Order Management check about the item?
options: Nothing — any item can be added to any order
That the item is enabled for the customer and for the ship-from warehouse
Only that the item has a barcode
That the item was manufactured this year
questions.explain: Order Management validates that the item is enabled for both the customer and the relevant ship-from organization.

questions.q: Why doesn't SO-48217 move straight into fulfillment after submission?
options: Because Harborview Industrial Supply is a brand-new customer
Because the item does not exist
Because of its size, it is flagged for a credit check before it can proceed
Because it has no ship-to site
questions.explain: The order's size triggers a credit check hold that must be reviewed and released, as covered in the next lessons.
